title: Bit bound as existence of an approximating protocol
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function of Alice's input and Bob's input, let $\varepsilon \in \bbr$ be an error parameter, and let $m \in \bbn$. Then the $\varepsilon$-error public-coin communication complexity satisfies $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le m$ if and only if there exist a length $n \in \bbn$ and a public-coin protocol $p$ over the coin tape $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$ and the worst-case bit complexity of $p$ is at most $m$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is a two-argument function
ε is a real error parameter
m is a natural number bound
conclusion: complexity ≤ m iff there exists n and a protocol on CoinTape(n) that ε-computes f with complexity ≤ m
replaced:
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$, and $m \in \mathbb{N}$,
we have $\mathrm{R}^{\mathrm{pub}}_\varepsilon(f) \le m$ if and only if there exist
$n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a public-coin protocol $p$ on $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$ such that
$p$ $\varepsilon$-approximates $f$ and $p.\mathrm{complexity} \le m$.
